newsitem.title: USA: AirTouch sees international profits in 1997.
newsitem.headline: AirTouch sees international profits in 1997.

text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc on Wednesday predicted that it would break into profits in its international operations for the first time in 1997, and expected capital spending of $1.2 billion in the year.
The company said that it expected to add at least as many customers on a proportionate basis in 1997 as the 1.6 million it added in 1996.
"We expect our international business to be profitable in 1997," Chief Executive Sam Ginn told a teleconference. "We will commit about 1.2 billion (dollars) of capital," he added.
AirTouch's capital spending in 1996 was $1.1 billion.
The company ended 1996 with 8,032,000 proportionate wireless customers. Proportionate accounting is used because of the company's large number of joint ventures.
Despite the spending, Ginn predicted that AirTouch's balance sheet would not be strained.
"We will maintain our credit rating and keep our debt under $2 billion (in 1997)," he said.
Ginn said that AirTouch's penetration of its U.S. markets was around 16 percent of the population covered, in Europe the figure was eight percent, and the figure in Asia was lower.
Ginn did not give an overall figure for Asia, but he noted that some areas stood out.
"Japan in one year grew from six percent to 17 percent (penetration in the company's markets)," he said.
Overall company cash flow would rise to $1.5 billion in 1997 from $1.1 billion in 1996, he predicted.
The company said its short-term debt is rated A2P2, and its long term debt BBB+. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
